question: Does hell exist?
summary: The Bible offers four mutually incompatible afterlife schemes. The apocalyptic strand (Daniel 12, Matthew, Mark, Luke, 2 Thessalonians, Hebrews, Jude, Revelation) describes eternal conscious torment. The annihilationist strand (Psalms, Proverbs, Obadiah, Romans, Galatians, Philippians, James) describes the wicked being destroyed, perishing, and ceasing to exist. The universalist strand (1 Cor 15:22, 1 Tim 4:10, 1 John 2:2) has all humans made alive in Christ. And the Sheol-only strand (Job, Psalms, Qohelet, Isaiah 38) has everyone going to the same silent dust regardless of moral state. Critical scholarship reads this as four overlapping historical layers, not one coherent doctrine.

reconcile.connective: Adam Clarke reads Paul's "everlasting destruction" as an eternal conscious state under judgment, not extinction of being.

discrepancy.connective: Historian Bart Ehrman argues the Bible preserves genuinely incompatible afterlife views: Sheol's finality, Daniel's resurrection, an annihilationist strand in Jesus and Paul, and Revelation's eternal torment.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's chapter 'Future Punishment — Its Nature' directly rebuts the annihilationist reading of 2 Thessalonians 1:9 and the row's other 'perish/destroy/consume/cut off' texts (Daniel 12:2, Matthew 13:41-42, 22:13, 25:41, Mark 9:43-48, Revelation 14:10-11, 20:15), arguing at length that none of them require extinction of consciousness.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: It is not annihilation, for their being continues; and as the destruction is everlasting, it is an eternal continuance and presence of substantial evil, and absence of all good …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly rejects the annihilationist reading of 'everlasting destruction,' asserting the wicked's conscious existence continues forever under judgment — the reconcile pole's core move, reading the destruction texts as compatible with eternal conscious torment rather than the Sheol/annihilation strands.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Who shall be punished - What this everlasting destruction consists in we cannot tell. It is not annihilation, for their being continues; and as the destruction is everlasting, it is an eternal continuance and presence of substantial evil, and absence of all good; for a part of this punishment consists in being banished from the presence of the Lord - excluded from his approbation, for ever; so that the light of his countenance can be no more enjoyed, as there will be an eternal impossibility of ever being reconciled to him.
The glory of his power - Never to see the face of God throughout eternity is a heart-rending, soul-appalling thought; and to be banished from the glory of his power, that power the glory of which is peculiarly manifested in saving the lost and glorifying the faithful, is what cannot be reflected on without confusion and dismay. But this must be the lot of all who acknowledge not God, and obey not the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.
